scope: Tests and CI only; no engine or published engine result changed. Native targeted measurements on this worktree.

vm22.source: The beam-column approximation already encoded in validation_ansys_vm22_cantilever_axial_bending: 1/(1-N/Pcr). This is a first-mode amplification approximation, not an exact cantilever solution or a verified ANSYS table.
vm22.uncertainty: Mesh refinement leaves a 0.13344% discrepancy against the approximate amplification. A 0.2% bound covers the measured approximation error and numerical margin; it replaces 15%.

vm40.source: Nanakorn and Vu (2006), Finite Elements in Analysis and Design 42, Table 1, printed p.1245; https://www.imechanica.org/sites/default/files/1-s2.0-S0168874X06000953-main.pdf . Independent elliptic-integral references and source locators in spec/mattiasson-1.json and spec/mattiasson-1-shortening.json.
vm40.uncertainty: The old 0.3015/0.0566 reference pair was not the audited table pair. Use the existing independent reference (0.301720773799814/0.056433236283377). The test has finite axial stiffness EA*L^2/EI=1200; refinement approaches an extensible solution, not the inextensible reference. Coarse-mesh errors decrease and retain a model difference. Bounds 0.1% for deflection and 0.6% for shortening cover the measured combined error, replacing 10% and 15%.

craig_bampton.source: The unreduced finite-element generalized eigenproblem on the identical 20-element cantilever, not an independent published frequency. Craig and Bampton (1968), Coupling of substructures for dynamic analyses, DOI 10.2514/3.4741, supplies the reduction method.
craig_bampton.uncertainty: Interior-mode truncation; five to eight retained modes reduces the worst error. The existing separate three-to-eight-mode convergence test remains and its eight-mode cap is also tightened. The new 0.03% cap covers the five-mode worst error with less than a 1.26 factor.

notional_load.source: The same frame under explicit notional loads and prescribed geometric lean; AISC 360-22 Appendix 1 is the existing formulation source. This is a cross-method consistency test, not a table of exact displacements.
notional_load.uncertainty: The small-lean approximation equates the two methods only to leading order; this discrete one-element-per-member frame measures an approximation difference. The 0.6% bound covers the measured 0.465914912% difference with a factor below 1.29, replacing 50%. No claim of exact equality or general mesh convergence.

shell_thermal.source: Uniform thermal strain gives the affine displacement alpha*deltaT*L already encoded by the test. This affine solution is representable on the existing regular quad patch.
shell_thermal.uncertainty: No discretisation allowance is needed for an affine patch; a 1e-8 relative roundoff allowance replaces 15%. Stress and out-of-plane checks stay in force.

mixed_frame_shell.source: Global force balance against the applied load totals in benchmark_mixed_frame_shell_building; this is conservation, not a published displacement reference.
mixed_frame_shell.uncertainty: A 1e-8 relative roundoff allowance replaces 15%; equilibrium is independent of mesh convergence.

navier.source: Kirchhoff double sine series, cross-checked against the rounded 1.28375 mm in Navier/Timoshenko plate benchmark sources recorded in research/benchmarks/navier-plate/README.md. Hard-support Mindlin comparison is a separate existing test.
navier.uncertainty: DKT errors decrease at approximately second order. MITC4 soft simple support differs from the hard-support series boundary-value problem; its nonmonotone errors are case-specific comparison bounds, not convergence to Kirchhoff. The existing hard-support and series-convergence checks are preserved without running the large 32/64 grids for this change.

shb8.source: MacNeal and Harder (1985), A proposed standard set of problems to test finite element accuracy, Table 8; DOI 10.1016/0168-874X(85)90003-4. The case references are unchanged.
shb8.uncertainty: Strong trapezoidal and parallelogram in-plane parasitic shear locking persists at the six-element mesh. The normalized measured values in macneal_harder.json /solidCantilever/regression are implementation regression pins with a 1e-5 relative drift bound, not accuracy claims. All previous lower and upper bounds remain enforced. No convergence or published equivalence is inferred from those pins.
